title: Building a game for yourself vs. one to market are different things
author: AuthorMaterial7495
selftext:
This is probably the biggest gap in knowledge I see here.

Almost every post in this sub is asking for feedback on a game someone made who's entire audience consists of themselves.

There's nothing wrong with making a game for yourself and honestly that should be most peoples approach because you really don't have the skills to make something good enough people will pay money for.    
  
 I'm making a super niche GTA style game that takes place on the street I live on in Denver.    
  
I'm not deluding myself into thinking people would want to play this game when there are AAA titles that do every aspect better than I'm going to be able to.   I'm doing it because I thought it would be fun to stage a game on the street I live on and see the actual businesses around me in a game engine.

There is 0 world where people are going to care about this game outside of myself. 

If my goal was to make something that could potentially sell or at least get players I'd be asking myself the following questions

* Which AI games have had any success and have sold?
* What are non traditional games that don't need to be sold on steam?
* What advantages does AI development have over traditional games?
* What games can you make that rely less on obviously AI assets (sound design, character animation, writing)?
* What's a concept that looks fun if you show a 5 second clip of the gameplay?

I can 100% tell you that it's not going to be your indie action RPG game with clunky animation and dialogue written by AI based on some grand idea you have. 

If your goal if more aligned around people actually liking and testing what you are creating, shoot for the next [worms.io](http://worms.io) , some sort of game using real data (think geoguesser/quiz games) or something like SuperHexagon that's a very simple concept not relying on the art/story/etc. and do it extremely well.
